ai.description: The Malabar Flying Frog (Rhacophorus malabaricus) is a large, vibrant green frog with red-webbed feet. It reaches 8–10 cm and features distinctive white spots and elongated, fully webbed toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Malabar Flying Frog is best distinguished by its vibrant, bright red webbing between the fingers and toes, which contrasts sharply with the green limbs.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Flying Frog inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen tropical forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near water bodies at elevations between 500 and 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The Malabar flying frog is primarily nocturnal and uses its expansive, webbed feet to glide between trees, allowing it to escape predators or hunt for insects mid-air.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Malabar flying frog breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying 60–100 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar flying frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at elevations up to 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar flying frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" calls, typically heard emanating from vegetation overhanging water bodies during the monsoon.
